title: Machine learning guides a proposed UCd3 intermetallic phase assignment
summary: A support-vector classifier using composition-derived elemental features predicted a Cu₃Au-type structure for UCd₃ and guided synthesis. Powder X-ray diffraction from the second of two samples showed peaks the authors fit to a UCd₃ phase with a = 4.648(2) Å; the sample also contained uranium, uranium oxide and cadmium, while the first sample differed. This is the authors’ proposed phase assignment from a multiphase powder, not phase-pure material or independent structural confirmation.
ai_technology: Support-vector machine discriminant analysis; Gaussian-process regression for feature completion
organization: The Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art; Manhattan College

source_review.scope: Primary ChemRxiv v1 full text, affiliation/date metadata, methods and diffraction discussion, plus primary UCd11 literature review for prior-compound context.

evidence.tested: The authors report synthesis and powder X-ray diffraction; the proposed phase was present in the second of two samples.
evidence.unknown: Only one synthesis batch/sample (the second of two samples) showed the additional peaks assigned by the authors to UCd₃; the powder was multiphase. The checked 2022 primary review says UCd₁₁ was the only previously reported U-Cd compound, but this is not an independent confirmation of the proposed UCd₃ structure.
evidence.ai_role: SVM classification of composition-derived descriptors predicted a Cu₃Au-type structure and motivated experimental synthesis/testing.
